prompt: An email filter sorts each message into spam or not spam.
why: Each email goes into one of two fixed categories: spam or not spam. Predicting a category from a known list is classification.
trap: The categories are fixed in advance, so it isn't clustering.

prompt: An app looks at a photo and says cat, dog or bird.
why: The answer is one label picked from a known list of three. Choosing among known categories is classification.

prompt: A bank predicts whether a loan will be repaid: yes or no.
why: The prediction is yes or no, not an amount. Choosing between known categories is classification.
trap: Repaid or not isn't a number on a scale.

prompt: A model tags customer reviews as positive, negative or neutral.
why: Each review gets one of three labels decided in advance: positive, negative or neutral. That's classification.
trap: The labels are chosen in advance.

prompt: A doctor's tool predicts which of five known skin conditions a photo shows.
tells: which of five known skin conditions
why: The tool picks which of five known conditions a photo shows. Assigning one of known categories is classification.
trap: It's running a model, but the task is classification.

prompt: A support bot routes each ticket to billing, technical or sales.
why: Each ticket goes to one of three known queues. Sorting items into fixed categories is classification.
trap: Clustering would find groups nobody named yet.
